files.why: Only source file; contains popup/modal markup, its CSS positioning and z-index versus the sticky header, and the logic that opens it

diagnosis.root_cause: The transform: translateZ(0) on <main> creates a stacking context that traps the modal's z-index: 9999 inside <main>, so the sticky header's root-level z-index: 100 paints over the modal's top.
diagnosis.suspect_function: CSS main rule (modal opened by the anonymous setTimeout callback)
diagnosis.mechanism: Because a transformed ancestor establishes a stacking context, the modal's z-index 9999 is only compared with siblings inside <main>; in the root stacking context the whole <main> subtree (z-index auto) is painted as one unit below the positioned sticky <header> (z-index 100), so whenever the absolutely-positioned modal's title bar reaches/overlaps the header area the header occludes that top strip despite the modal's nominally larger z-index.
diagnosis.test_spec: Load the page, wait >1s for #backdrop.open, then scroll so the modal title overlaps the sticky header (or measure in the overlap region) and record #modalTitle.getBoundingClientRect(), #hdr.getBoundingClientRect(), and document.elementFromPoint() at the modal title's center-top point plus the hit-testable/visible fraction of the title's height. Correct behavior: elementFromPoint returns #modalTitle and the visible title fraction is 1.0 (full title height); reported behavior: elementFromPoint returns #hdr and the visible title fraction drops below 1.0 by the header-overlap amount while the modal is open.

fix_strategies.name: Portal the modal to body level
fix_strategies.approach: Move the #backdrop/#modal markup out of <main> to be a direct child of <body> (or append it to document.body on open) so its z-index 9999 competes in the root stacking context against the header's 100 instead of being confined inside <main>.

fix_strategies.name: Remove the stacking context from main
fix_strategies.approach: Delete the transform: translateZ(0) from the main rule (or apply it only while no modal is open / replace the compositing hint with one that does not create a stacking context), restoring global z-index comparison so the modal's 9999 beats the header's 100.

fix_strategies.name: Promote the modal to the top layer
fix_strategies.approach: Render the popup with a native top-layer API, e.g. a <dialog> opened via showModal() (or the Popover API), which paints above all stacking contexts including the sticky header regardless of the transformed ancestor, keeping <main>'s transform intact.
